regime.label: Germany - domestic B2B e-invoicing, and XRechnung into the public sector over Peppol
regime.scope: Every domestic company must already be able to receive a B2B electronic invoice, with no turnover threshold. The duty to issue one is the part that is still phasing in, by prior-year turnover.

commencement.notes: No threshold. The receiving duty landed on everyone at once.

regime.notes: The Leitweg-ID travels as the buyer reference (BT-10) and public-sector receivers reject without it. Germany has no reporting leg: the source above states there is no real-time reporting system, which is why this stays a network country and does not become a hybrid one. The label said public sector only until the domestic B2B receiving duty had been in force for over a year. Both future phases are recorded as enacted on the European Commission's characterisation of the timetable, not on a reading of the German statute itself.
